roadmap_acceptance_criteria.text: New and reconciled US-listed securities use stable FIGI-domain keys where applicable, issuer identity is separate from security identity, effective-dated listing/provider-symbol history is retained, and unresolved candidates are quarantined without silent merges.
Canonical bars distinguish instrument, market/feed scope, session, timeframe, adjustment basis/version, and provenance; existing OHLCV reads remain compatible through a default series mapping.
Exchange sessions, timezones, holidays, early closes, overnight trade-date rules, and user-local projections are versioned and used by freshness and daily-completion logic.

Provider routing filters by capability, asset/venue/session/interval/history/feed/terms entitlement, health, quota, and workload budget; quota reservations are safe across workers and every decision is observable.

Whole-universe core-session D1 refresh, tiered intraday polling, local rollups, exact missing-slice repair, request coalescing, deferred broad-evaluator runs, and automatic retry are implemented without provider calls inside evaluation loops.

Provider adapters cover the approved practical roster, with US identity/lifecycle, OHLCV, corporate actions, market events, SEC facts/core fundamentals, earnings, FINRA short interest, crypto, current options, and optional futures paths represented honestly by capability and provenance.

Current option chains and quotes are retained; QuantLib-backed American-option Greeks and the existing fallback are labeled with model/version/input provenance and tested against numerical edge cases.

Backend-only admin and diagnostic APIs expose capabilities, entitlements, quota/cost usage, routing decisions, coverage, identity quarantine, sessions, queue/degradation state, anomalies, and detailed shadow reports.

New routing defaults remain disabled until a separately approved deployed 30-day shadow run produces automated daily/final reports, at least 99% eligible core-session D1 coverage before the next regular session, no silent identity/license/quota violations, and AI-readable discrepancy evidence.
Existing symbol-based API aliases and legacy yfinance-dependent paths remain functional only through explicit compatibility behavior; yfinance is absent from default and acceptance routing.

Focused unit, adapter-fixture, migration, PostgreSQL/Redis integration, worker, API, numerical, point-in-time, and full backend integration validation pass; every live-enabled provider has either bounded keyless evidence or an explicit credential preflight failure; no frontend files are modified.

No provider policy contains a generic 60/min, 15-burst, 2-concurrency, or 30-second fallback. Unknown limits are represented as NULL/unknown, excluded from routing, and surfaced with the exact missing contract dimensions.

429/418/quota responses parse provider reset headers where present, stop the affected provider scope, persist a typed capacity event, defer work until the reset (or operator decision), and do not create a retry storm or unsafe fallback.

The manifest-driven live matrix covers keyless and credentialed providers separately. Missing credentials identify exact environment variables and block ready-for-review; no live skip is represented as proof.

Local development, GitHub staging validation, GitHub master validation, and live/production each use separate explicit secret stores; current local keys are never copied to CI; no credential is tracked or exposed in routine PR CI/artifacts/logs; provider credentials reach only trusted backend/worker processes.

Every registered external provider capability has a source-backed, versioned contract for plan, authentication scope, exact quota units/windows/resets/shared pools, operation costs, pagination, response bytes, history/venue/freshness, and data-use rights; provider documentation, account endpoints, and live headers are reconciled, and verified limits are not left unknown or incorrectly gated.

The owner has granted blanket approval for private durable storage of data returned by all providers; do not request per-provider owner approval again. Provider authentication, account entitlements, quotas, and any explicit provider or embedded third-party restrictions remain separate provider facts and must be reported accurately rather than described as missing owner consent.

Provider usage reservations survive process/session restart and coordinate all workers sharing the same account scope; local worktrees share an owner-only local ledger, deployments use shared durable runtime storage, and CI attempts reconcile prior redacted receipts and worst-case interrupted usage before spending shared credentials.

Complete US-listed equity/ETF reconciliation must cover distinct official listing-source scopes rather than treating Nasdaq Trader's two files as the whole market. Include CTA Plan's daily Tape A/B symbol file (preserve prior symbols and every source row; parse instrument type and primary listing participant code) and Nasdaq's Nasdaq-listed/Tape C roster; retain Nasdaq Trader's two files as valuable supplementary/cross-check evidence, not sole whole-NMS authority. Verify each source's full pagination/file integrity, date/generation evidence, participant-code-to-MIC mappings, and venue coverage before it can contribute absence evidence. Combine only same-session, individually complete source scopes for universe-wide lifecycle decisions; partial or stale source runs may add observations but may not count absence. Preserve every OTC source row/page from FINRA's official Query API otcSecurityMaster dataset, live-verified against the public Symbol Directory, plus FINRA Daily List lifecycle deltas. Commit each SEC issuer response, candidate, failure-retry state, and next cursor atomically per CIK so a restart never re-fetches completed CIKs; test totals, cursor completion, duplicate detection, stable partition dates, ticker changes, and three-distinct-complete-snapshot-day deactivation evidence. A partial snapshot is never authoritative and no relevant provider row may be silently discarded.

SEC directory scans first stage a complete report with issuer creation disabled; after that exact clean report is reviewed, a bounded no-refetch operation materializes only validated missing CIK/name issuer rows from retained source payloads, while likely future listings become inactive provisional instruments only on strong unambiguous evidence and all ambiguous evidence is quarantined.

External-service code changes are enforced by repository workflow checks requiring provider/capability declaration, contract evidence, fixture tests, bounded current-source live tests, secret scope, usage impact, and explicit deferral status; future changes cannot silently bypass the live-validation policy.

Dinari Sandbox may run only through a separately capped canary; every returned response payload is retained in the owner-private redacted response archive, while Sandbox observations never enter canonical production data, usage, alert, or analytics tables. Dinari production routing remains disabled under the approved free-only budget.

The 30-day deployed shadow run remains disabled and is not part of the current implementation phase; after every other controllable acceptance gate is complete, it will be planned and authorized as the final gate before human closure and staging integration.
